value.subtitle: Pairing a connected light with a phone — the part of a hardware product where people quietly give up.

hero.alt: COSMO Connected onboarding and pairing flow
hero.caption: The full pairing flow — prototype recording

sections.heading: Which device is in your hand?
sections.body: The range covers several products, and a pairing flow that guesses will fail for the wrong reason — leaving the user convinced the hardware is broken. So the first question is the plain one, asked once, in the words printed on the box.

images.alt: Device selection screen asking which Cosmo product is being paired
images.caption: Ask first, in the words on the box.

sections.heading: Bluetooth, without the anxiety
sections.body: Searching, found, connected — then “click to test”. That last step is the one that matters: the user confirms the pairing with their own eyes, by seeing the light react, instead of trusting a spinner that claims success. When a device fails to appear, the screen says what to check rather than looping.

images.alt: Connection screen confirming the device is connected, with a test action
images.caption: Confirmation you can see, not a spinner you must believe.

sections.heading: The physical half of the flow
sections.body: Half of this onboarding happens with two hands on a bike: mounting the unit, aligning it, checking visibility. Those steps are drawn rather than photographed, because line art stays legible on a phone held in the street, in daylight, at arm’s length.

images.alt: Line-art illustration of the light unit clipping onto its saddle mount, above the installation screen heading
images.caption: Drawn, not photographed — legibility beats realism outdoors.

sections.heading: Then the remote, the same way
sections.body: The handlebar remote reuses the pattern exactly: same sequence, same wording, same confirmation. Learning the flow once should be enough to add any device in the range — including the ones that did not exist when it was designed.

images.caption: One pattern, reused for every device.
